input.brief:
Two-panel figure explaining what a manifold is, with four elements.

PANEL A (left, larger): the unit circle in the plane, centre at origin, radius 1, drawn as a grey thick curve. Two overlapping CHART ARCS drawn in different colours on top of it:
- Chart 1 in blue: the arc from angle -135° to +135° (i.e. the circle minus the top-left..top-right gap), drawn slightly offset outward from the circle so it reads as a separate stroke.
- Chart 2 in red: the arc from angle 45° to 315° going the other way (the circle minus a gap at the top), also offset slightly inward so both arcs remain visible where they overlap.
Shade the two overlap regions (around angle -45° and +135°) with a light hatch or tint, and label one of them "overlap".
Label the arcs "chart 1: θ ∈ (-3π/4, 3π/4)" and "chart 2" respectively, in their colours.
Mark a point P on the circle at angle 30° with a filled dot, labelled "P". Draw the TANGENT LINE at P as a dashed black line, and label it "tangent at P — a 1-plane". Draw the radius from origin to P as a thin dotted line.
Add a short caption under the panel: "every point has an arc as a neighbourhood; the tangent line rotates as you go around".

PANEL B (right, smaller): the union of the two coordinate axes in the plane, drawn as thick grey lines. Circle a small disk around the origin with a red dashed outline, and inside that disk draw the four branches clearly meeting at the origin. Label the circled region "at the origin: no arc can cover a neighbourhood". Add a second small marker at a point on the positive x-axis, labelled "elsewhere: an arc works".
Caption under panel B: "xy = 0 — not a 1-manifold".

Overall: clean white background, restrained palette (grey curve, one blue, one red, black dashed tangent), axes with tick marks and labels x and y on both panels, equal aspect ratio in both so the circle is round. A single title at the top: "A 1-manifold: locally an interval, globally curved". Legible labels, no overlap.

result.notes: The figure is correct and clean. Notes: Panel A shows the unit circle with the blue chart θ ∈ (−3π/4, 3π/4) offset outward and the red complementary chart offset inward, tinted overlap arcs at θ ∈ [45°,135°] and [225°,315°] (labelled "overlap" on the upper one), point P at 30° with its dotted radius, dashed tangent line, and both captions. Panel B shows the cross xy = 0 with a dashed disk at the origin, darker branch segments meeting there, an "elsewhere" marker on the positive x-axis, and the caption — so the contrast "arc works everywhere on the circle vs. fails at the origin" reads at a glance.
